task_message:
Case N23: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 221x221x330 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
The case is complete. Final summary:

- **Target found:** a well-circumscribed, fusiform T2-hyperintense mass in the anterior subcutaneous/fascial plane of the limb, best seen on axial slices ~208–229, measuring roughly 26 × 18 × 41 mm (8.8 mL).
- **Segmentation:** seeded with a single positive point on the lesion core (axial 217); the model captured the whole mass, and a refine pass cleaned the boundary (single connected component, extent axial 198–239, coronal 138–156, sagittal 117–143).
- **Verification:** three-plane review confirmed the green outline follows the bright mass in all planes; the past-the-end slices (axi 190/247, cor 130/164, sag 109/151) showed no residual lesion tissue. The automatic candidate proposals (C1–C5) were thin bright fat/fascial sheets adjacent to the mass and were rejected as normal tissue.
- **Result:** final mask saved (medium confidence — main mass boundary is clear, with some uncertainty about the bright fascial/possible nerve tail at the deep margin).
